clue.text: Type of seat mostly used until now

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of the phrase, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: until now means so far, written as one run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the kind of chair they have mostly sat in up to the present.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered couch, a kind of seat for several people.

clue.text: Crabby type initially serving our queen, maybe

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of serving

parts.note: taken as written
a queen is a female cat, and puss is a word for a cat

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered person is first to wait on our monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty, but a queen is a female cat, here PUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sourpuss is a sullen, bad-tempered person, a grump.

clue.text: Series of steps taken to secure a new window

indicators.note: taken to secure means the steps hold the following letters within them

parts.note: a flight is a series of stairs

explanation.surface: A procedure is followed to install a replacement window.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a small semicircular window above a door.

clue.text: Well-founded evidence that's acceptable for recorder

parts.note: a well-founded argument is a sound one
evidence that settles a matter is proof

explanation.surface: Solid documentary evidence that a court recorder would accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' suggests a court official, but the definition means a room fit for making recordings, with no outside noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio for a recording engineer must be insulated against noise, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Wizard place! Ace for invigorating air!

parts.note: Oz is the land ruled by the Wizard in the famous children's story
an ace counts as one

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a magical land and its fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' reads as British slang for excellent, but it points to the land of the Wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside air is popularly but loosely called this, as if bracing.

clue.text: Upbeat when anticipating university gathering? Of course

parts.note: beat means tan (to thrash), and up, in a down clue, sends it upwards to read nat
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerful because a university reunion is coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upbeat' looks like cheerful, but it is split: up reverses beat (TAN). 'When anticipating' means coming before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb used as an interjection of agreement means certainly, without question.

clue.text: Sort of film, or match, abandoned in alarm

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the word for alarm

parts.note: panic is sudden alarm

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or uninhibited, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film plan or a sports match is dropped out of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as called off, but it scrambles OR MATCH into CHROMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Panchromatic photographic film is sensitive to all colours of visible light.

clue.text: Unique, holding exercises in public

indicators.note: holding means the word for unique wraps around the exercises

parts.note: an only child is unique, the one and only
PE, physical education, means exercises

explanation.surface: A one-off workout session is held in front of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in full view of others means doing it without concealment.

clue.text: Understand meaning of sound

definitions.meaning: to grasp or work out a meaning
to measure the depth of water

explanation.surface: Someone tries to grasp what a noise signifies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise, but it means to measure water depth; 'meaning of' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to comprehend and to measure depth, from the six-foot unit of depth.

clue.text: Sailors in American vessels

indicators.note: in places the sailors inside the abbreviation for American

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Navy men serving aboard American ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' looks like ships to go with the sailors, but the definition means containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, so they are vessels in the pottery sense.

clue.text: Body of troops originally garrisoned in Europe

indicators.note: in tells us the initial of garrisoned sits within the word for Europe

parts.note: Britons call mainland Europe the Continent

indicators.note: originally means take only the opening letter of garrisoned

explanation.surface: A detachment of soldiers first stationed on the European mainland.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group of soldiers contributed to a larger force.

clue.text: Admit being wrong keeping single weapon in a set, perhaps

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the other pieces inside
perhaps tells us a set is one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: single means one
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: Confessing an error while keeping one blade among a matching collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges A SET into EATS, which then holds ONE SWORD.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement humiliatingly is the idiom for conceding a mistake.

clue.text: Soldier escorting monarch into armed vessel

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the reigning queen

explanation.surface: A soldier accompanies the sovereign aboard a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escorting' and 'into' simply join the pieces: the soldier comes first, the monarch after.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a privately owned ship armed and licensed to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: Greeting, from eponymous Shakespearean. giving away books

indicators.note: giving away means the books are removed from the play's title character

parts.note: Othello is the title character of the Shakespeare play named after him
OT, the Old Testament, stands for books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A salutation offered by the Moor of a Shakespeare tragedy as he hands out volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the everyday word said when meeting someone, a common salutation.

clue.text: A comrade in the class struggle?

definitions.text: A comrade in the class struggle?

parts.words: A comrade in the class struggle?
parts.note: class struggle suggests Marxist politics and comrades, but read literally it is a companion in a school class battling through lessons

explanation.surface: A political ally fighting in the Marxist class war.
explanation.definitionFit: A classmate at the same school is a companion who shares the struggles of the classroom.

clue.text: Free to travel, though abandoned after short distance

indicators.note: after means the word for abandoned comes behind the short distance

parts.note: a foot is a short measure of length
loose means unrestrained, abandoned in behaviour

explanation.surface: Someone is at liberty to roam despite being left behind a little way.
explanation.definitionFit: Footloose means unattached and able to go wherever one likes.

clue.text: Imitate fan? Not the first time

indicators.note: not the first means the earlier of the two occurrences of the letter is removed

parts.note: to fan flames or interest is to stimulate it

explanation.surface: A copy of an enthusiast that is not a first attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like an admirer, but it is a verb meaning stimulate.
explanation.definitionFit: To simulate is to imitate or feign the appearance of something.

clue.text: Star set out to 'be involved in a venture

indicators.note: involved in means the jumbled letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: a risk is a venture with an uncertain outcome

indicators.note: out means the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity prepares to take part in a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' looks like starting off, but 'out' scrambles SET into STE, placed in A RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: This printed symbol is the typographic star used to mark footnotes.

clue.text: Scientific study to make change in car some day?

indicators.note: make change tells us to rearrange the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A forecast that a field of science will one day transform cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make change' turns IN CAR SOME DAY into the answer; note that 'in' is part of the fodder, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the branch of physics studying how air flows around moving bodies such as cars and aircraft.

clue.text: Put up with role as provincial governor

indicators.note: put up, in a down clue, means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates their position as a regional ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate, but 'Put up' reverses PART AS; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a governor of a province in ancient Persia.

clue.text: Depression perceptible when a member is elevated

definitions.text: Depression perceptible when a member is elevated

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
a pit is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: A hollow that shows only when a limb is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the member sits above the depression; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow beneath the shoulder shows when the limb is lifted.

clue.text: Missile knocking front off agricultural equipment

indicators.note: knocking front off means losing the opening letter of the farm tool

parts.note: a harrow is a farm implement for breaking up soil

explanation.surface: A projectile strikes and damages the front of a farm machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a projectile shot from a bow.

clue.text: Confusing us with details leads to weariness

indicators.note: confusing means the letters of us and details are jumbled

explanation.surface: Overloading people with fine points leaves them tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental fatigue, a lack of energy.

clue.text: Fitzgerald's inn, briefly enclosed by these railings

indicators.note: enclosed by means the letters sit inside the words these railings

explanation.surface: A Victorian translator's inn is fenced in by these railings.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Fitzgerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam speaks of 'this battered Caravanserai'; 'briefly' trims that to its short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai is a caravanserai, an Eastern inn for travellers, here in shortened form.

clue.text: All the pieces one knows of French

definitions.text: All the pieces one knows of French

parts.words: All the pieces one knows of French
parts.note: the full stock of musical or dramatic works a performer can give, named with a word taken from French

explanation.surface: Every passage of French a learner can recall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of French' points to the word's origin, French répertoire; 'pieces' means works a performer has ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's stock of works ready to play is their range of available pieces.

clue.text: Make heavy demands on one's transport

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain or burden them
one is the Roman numeral I, with the 's meaning has

explanation.surface: Someone's car proves a strain on their resources.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a hired car, a form of transport.

clue.text: Irishman is given Republic's backing to create shop

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name in crosswords

indicators.note: backing means the Republic's name, with its possessive S, is read in reverse

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland, plus S for the possessive

explanation.surface: An Irishman funded by the Irish state opens a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like financial support, but it reverses EIRES to give SERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a cake shop selling French pastries.

clue.text: Pack platform

definitions.meaning: a pack of playing cards is also called this
a ship's floor or a raised level surface

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a set of playing cards and a ship's flat floor.
